Fit the backward joint model with censored subjects in the longitudinal sub-model

Source: R/fitImputedBJM.R
fitImputedBJM.Rd

Experimental. The usual right-censored fit estimates the longitudinal sub-model \(f(Y \mid T)\) on the subjects with an observed event only. That is valid when censoring is independent of \((T, Y)\), but \(f(Y \mid T)\) is then learned only over the event times seen among the events, which are the early ones when many subjects are censored. Prediction needs \(f(Y \mid T)\) for every \(T\) after the prediction time, so for a patient doing well it extrapolates the event-time effect beyond the data. With a large censored fraction this shifts the predictive distribution of \(T\) towards early events: risks are overestimated, increasingly so at later landmarks, and in short follow-up the ranking of patients can be lost too.

fitImputedBJM() also uses the censored subjects, who carry the information on long event times. It fills in their \(T > C\) by stochastic EM, then by multiple imputation, as fitIntervalBJM does for interval censoring:

  1. fit the survival sub-model (survivalSub()) once, and the longitudinal sub-model on the subjects with an event (the usual fit);

  2. draw each censored subject's \(T\) from \(f(T \mid T > C, Y, X) \propto f(Y \mid T, X) f(T \mid X)\) (imputeEventTime()); with competing risks, draw the event type \(D\) jointly, from \(f(Y \mid T, D) P(D \mid T) f(T)\);

  3. refit longitudinalSub() on all subjects and repeat for n_burnin iterations;

  4. keep iterating, saving every n_thin-th fit until n_imputations are saved, and pool them for prediction (see poolLongitudinalSub).

The marginal survival model is the usual one (or the one passed in survival_fit_all) and is fit once. With competing risks the event-type model \(P(D \mid T)\) is by default refit on every draw, on the subjects with an event and the censored subjects with their drawn \((T, D)\), and averaged over the imputations. The draws of \(T\) beyond the last follow-up rely on the survival model's tail: the extrapolated one by default, or one borrowed from an external cohort with longer follow-up (survivalSubExternal).

Using the censored subjects makes the event-time effect matter where it was never observed, so a term linear in \(T\) can drift over the long event times now in the fit. A bounded effect, e.g. I(exp(-years / 5)) in place of years in every term of long_sub_fixed, levels off for long \(T\); choose its scale by comparing observedLongLogLik across candidate fits. On pbc3 (landmarks 1-3 years, 3-year window), the usual fit overestimates the cumulative incidence of death by 8-32\ cross-validation and this fit with exp(-years / 5) by -1 to 7\ with the same AUC.

Usage

fitImputedBJM(
  data_survival,
  data_fit_all,
  form_marginal_surv,
  long_sub_fixed,
  long_sub_random,
  time_variable,
  form_conditional_cr = NULL,
  survival_variable_all = NULL,
  survival_trans_function = NULL,
  n_burnin = 5,
  n_imputations = 5,
  n_thin = 2,
  n_grid = 40,
  baseline = c("spline", "piecewise"),
  df = NULL,
  survival_fit_all = NULL,
  refit_event_type = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data_survival

One row per subject: event or censoring time, event indicator, the survival covariates and the subject id.

data_fit_all

As in longitudinalSub: one data frame per biomarker (or one shared data frame), long format, for every subject, with the event (or censoring) time in the column used in long_sub_fixed. The censored subjects' event-time column, event-type column and the columns named in survival_variable_all are (re)filled from the draws.

form_marginal_surv, form_conditional_cr

As in survivalSub: Surv(time, status) ~ covariates and the optional event-type model. The event-time variable of form_marginal_surv must be the one used in long_sub_fixed.

long_sub_fixed, long_sub_random

As in longitudinalSub.

time_variable

Name of the visit-time column.

survival_variable_all, survival_trans_function

Transformed event-time columns, as in predictRisk (NULL if none).

n_burnin

Stochastic-EM iterations before fits are saved.

n_imputations

Number of saved fits.

n_thin

Iterations between saved fits.

n_grid

Grid points per subject for the draws.

baseline, df

Baseline hazard of the survival model (see survivalSub).

survival_fit_all

Optional right-censored survival sub-model to use instead of fitting one from form_marginal_surv and form_conditional_cr, e.g. from survivalSubExternal. form_marginal_surv is still used to read each subject's time and status in data_survival.

refit_event_type

With competing risks, refit the event-type model on every draw (see Description); FALSE keeps the one fit on the subjects with an event.

seed

Optional integer seed (the global RNG state is restored).

Value

An object of class "fitImputedBJM", a list with survival_fit_all (with competing risks and refit_event_type, its event-type coefficients averaged over the imputations; survival_fit_all_list has one per imputation); long_fit_all (the imputations combined, for predictRisk() and friends); long_fit_all_list (one fit per imputation); pooled (poolLongitudinalSub of the fits, when n_imputations > 1); imputed_T (and, with competing risks, imputed_D), censored subjects x imputations; trace (each iteration's fixed effects, to check the chain has settled); and settings. print() shows a short summary.

See also

observedLongLogLik to compare fits; fitIntervalBJM for interval-censored event times.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(pbc3)
pbc3_surv <- pbc3[!duplicated(pbc3$id), ]
fit <- fitImputedBJM(pbc3_surv, pbc3, Surv(years, status3) ~ age + sex,
                     long_sub_fixed = serBilir ~ year + age + sex +
                       I(exp(-years / 5)) + I(year * exp(-years / 5)),
                     long_sub_random = ~ year | id, time_variable = "year",
                     n_burnin = 2, n_imputations = 2, n_thin = 1, seed = 1)
fit
#> 
#> Backward joint model with imputed censored event times (fitImputedBJM)
#> 
#>   169 subjects with an event, 143 censored with T imputed; 2 imputation(s) after 2 burn-in iterations, keeping every iteration
#> 
#> Longitudinal sub-model, pooled over the imputations (Rubin's rules):
#> 
#>   [1] Outcome 1
#>                         estimate std_error     fmi
#> (Intercept)              0.41810  0.257200 0.10160
#> year                     0.03166  0.012570 0.02159
#> age                     -0.01279  0.004084 0.11400
#> sex                     -0.05711  0.129900 0.05040
#> I(exp(-years/5))         2.61600  0.155200 0.02854
#> I(year * exp(-years/5))  0.70130  0.052980 0.06498
#> 
#> Use x$long_fit_all and x$survival_fit_all for prediction; x$trace to check the chain has settled.

# compare with the usual fit on the subjects with an event
usual <- longitudinalSub(pbc3[pbc3$status3 == 1, ],
                         list(serBilir ~ year + age + sex + years + years * year),
                         list(~ year | id))
observedLongLogLik(fit, pbc3_surv, pbc3, time_variable = "year")
#> [1] -1356.182
observedLongLogLik(list(long_fit_all = usual, survival_fit_all = fit$survival_fit_all),
                   pbc3_surv, pbc3, time_variable = "year")
#> [1] -1573.894

history <- pbc3[pbc3$id == 2 & pbc3$year <= 3, ]
predictRisk(history, fit$long_fit_all, fit$survival_fit_all,
            prediction_time = 3, horizon = 3, time_variable = "year",
            survival_variable_all = NULL, survival_trans_function = NULL,
            bandcount1 = 10, bandcount2 = 10)
#> 
#> =================================================================
#>  Dynamic Prediction - Event Risk
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#>   Competing risks   : No
#>   Subjects          : 1
#> -----------------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#>  Subject Risk Prob
#>        2    0.1777
#> 
#> =================================================================
#> 
# }
